claim_reviews.conclusion: “air conditioner” correctly matches a household appliance that cools indoor air.

claim_reviews.conclusion: “AC” is an ordinary Indonesian abbreviation for air conditioner/air conditioning and matches the intended appliance sense.
claim_reviews.subject: Indonesian answer: AC

claim_reviews.conclusion: “pendingin hawa” is a valid Malaysian Malay term, but DBP characterizes it as an older term and identifies “penyaman udara” as the more precise/current term.

claim_reviews.conclusion: “different-common-word” is too strong without a register qualifier because AC/aircond may also occur in Malaysian usage; there is no false-friend contrast between the listed forms.
claim_reviews.subject: Final relation and false-friend contrast

rationale: The English cue and Indonesian answer are sound. Malaysian “pendingin hawa” is valid and understood, but Malaysian terminology guidance treats it as an older term and prefers “penyaman udara”; “aircond” is also common colloquially. The different-common-word relation therefore overstates the contrast, and no false-friend contrast is present.
